chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from one of our companions, from Al-Mu'alla Abu Uthman, from Abu Baseer, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'And Dawud and Sulaiman when they both gave judgement concerning the field when the people's sheep pastured therein.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The pasturing (nafash) does not occur except at night. Indeed, it is upon the owner of the field to protect the field during the day, and it is not upon the owner of the cattle to protect it during the day.'

Rather, their grazing and sustenance are during the day. So whatever they spoil [during the day], there is no blame upon them. And it is upon the owners of the cattle to protect the cattle from the fields of the people at night. So whatever they spoil at night, they are responsible for it, and that is the 'nafash'.

And indeed Dawud (peace be upon him) judged that the owner of the crop should receive the necks of the sheep, and Sulayman (peace be upon him) judged that he should receive the 'risl' and 'thallath', which is the milk and the wool, for that year.

key_terms.الثَّلَّةَ: A quantity or flock, referring here to the yield of milk and wool.
key_terms.الرِّسْلُ: A term referring to the young or the first offspring, often used in the context of milk or wool yield.
key_terms.النَّفَشُ: Night grazing or pasturing, specifically referring to the time when animals are not typically watched, leading to damage.
key_terms.رِقَابَ الْغَنَمِ: The necks of the sheep, referring to the principal value or the animals themselves as compensation.
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْحَرْثِ: The owner of the field or crop.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on liability for livestock damaging crops during the day versus at night?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the jurisprudential principles derived from the Quranic narrative of Dawud and Sulayman (AS), clarifying the distinction between 'nafash' (night grazing) and day grazing to assign liability for crop damage. It establishes that while the field owner bears the duty of protection during daylight hours when animals are actively grazing, the animal owner is liable for damages occurring at night, a ruling that underscores the concept of 'daman' (guarantee/responsibility) in Shia fiqh. The narration further details the specific compensation awarded by the Prophets, distinguishing between the value of the livestock ('riqab') and the produce ('risl'), reflecting the nuanced legal reasoning attributed to Sulayman's wisdom.
